newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC sees case for steady EU grain set-aside rate.
newsitem.headline: ONIC sees case for steady EU grain set-aside rate.

text.p: Strong world demand for European Union grain helped the EU absorb a good part of its bumper 1996 crop, making a case for holding the set-aside rate for the 1998 grain harvest at the current five percent, the head of France's grain office ONIC said on Wednesday.

Director-general Alain Moulinier said that because of strong demand for EU grain within and outside the European Union, the EU may end the 1996/97 campaign with grain intervention stocks lower than some operators had initially feared.
"EU grain intervention stocks may not be at the levels some feared a few months ago," Moulinier said.
He said that members of ONIC's permanent committee expected the EU to have seven to eight million tonnes of grain in its intervention stores at end June 1997.
"This is an interesting start to negotiate a set-aside rate for next year," he added.
Asked what set-aside rate would be desirable, Moulinier said "operators want the lowest possible set-aside rate, that is around this year's level of five percent."
Logistical hurdles plaguing some of its rivals led the European Union to substantially raise wheat exports in recent weeks, Moulinier said.
"There is no doubt that market dynamics fed by difficulties experienced by our rivals led the Commission to take advantage of the situation and go beyond what it initially planned," he said.
"The Commission was generous during the last four weeks," he said, adding the EU granted exports for 1.24 million tonnes of soft wheat while substantially cutting export subsidies.
Sales clinched last month have led ONIC to raise its target for French 1996/97 soft wheat exports to non-EU countries by 150,000 tonnes to 6.4 million tonnes.
"This adjustment seems justified in view of new sales made last month," he said.
Moulinier said business included a contract for 200,000 tonnes of wheat to Algeria, 300,000 tonnes of wheat to Iran and unspecified wheat sales to Cuba.
The EU has granted licences to export 8.1 million tonnes of soft wheat grain since the start of the 1996/97 season against 5.3 million tonnes in the previous season.
